report.summary: The storehouse level 2 upgrade was committed and is now active, with 11 game minutes left. The earlier affordability check is stale: after the 60 iron and 30 silver charge, ordinary stocks are about 28.07 iron and 6.33 silver, so another upgrade is not currently affordable. Your iron-for-grain contract with Sim Farmer 81 is active for 49 more game minutes; it has delivered 360 marked units of each resource so far, with no overflow or failed installments.
report.whatChanged: Receipt truth confirms the storehouse upgrade was queued and charged, and the after-state shows construction active. The mine, market, and farm upgrades listed in the history are finished. Two other supply proposals are open and unsigned: one would send 3 silver/hour for 3 iron/hour, the other would send 3 iron/hour for 3 grain/hour. They are proposed only; neither is signed or active. No action is shown as rejected. The contact requests list is empty.
report.nextDecision: Once the storehouse finishes, compare available upgrade costs and projected production before choosing another investment. The current iron-for-grain contract is active; the proposals remain unsigned, and the mandate allows signing but does not allow making or changing offers.
report.reasonToReturn: Return when the storehouse completes or the active contract ends, to reassess costs, production, and whether either open proposal is worth signing.
report.confusion: The plan says the storehouse was affordable, but the later stock check marks it unaffordable because that check reflects the post-charge state while the upgrade is already busy. Also, the plan described the active trade as iron for grain, which matches the actual active contract; the open offers are different proposed trades.

report.summary: The message to Farmer 72 was sent successfully. Your existing one-hour deal with Farmer 12 is still active and has about 25 game minutes left.
report.whatChanged: The receipt confirms the message was committed, so it is sent—not merely proposed or queued. It asks Farmer 72 whether they would consider a one-hour exchange of 3 iron per hour for 3 grain per hour after the Farmer 12 deal ends. No reply or new agreement is shown. The Farmer 12 contract is signed by both sides and active; the records show deliveries in both directions so far. Nothing here is marked rejected or queued, and no deal with Farmer 72 is finished or signed.
report.nextDecision: Keep the Farmer 12 promise through its remaining term. When it ends, check for Farmer 72's reply and the current offers and stock before agreeing to anything else.
report.reasonToReturn: Return after the active deal ends or Farmer 72 replies, so you can decide whether to make the follow-up trade.
report.confusion: The plan mentions a deal with Farmer 12 and a reply from Farmer 72, but the snapshot contains no Farmer 72 reply or offer. The active contract record identifies Farmer 12 as Farmer 12, while the contacts list uses a different handle for that kingdom.

report.summary: The market upgrade is finished, and the buyer inquiry was sent successfully. No trade is active.
report.whatChanged: Market level 2 is complete. Your message to Merchant 53 asking for exact Grain and Silver terms was committed; it is a request for details, not a trade agreement. Two one-hour offers remain open and signed only by the other side: one would send your Iron for Grain, and the other would send your Silver for Iron. Each requires you to deliver 3 per hour, while you currently have about 20.7 Iron and 10.5 Silver. No offer is signed by you, no supply contract is queued, and there are no active contracts. Neither offer is marked rejected or finished; both are still open and due to expire soon. No specific reply from Merchant 53 is shown.
